newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: TV giant CLT-UFA seeks Europe-wide expansion.
newsitem.headline: TV giant CLT-UFA seeks Europe-wide expansion.

text.p: CLT-UFA, the newly-founded Luxembourg-based European television group, said on Tuesday it wanted to expand its leading position in the free television market in Europe.
"In those countries where we are not the leader yet, we are trying to become the leader," CLT-UFA co-chief executive officer Remy Sautter told a news conference.
The expansion drive in both existing and new markets would involve heavy investment. "We plan to invest hundreds of millions of marks per year," Sautter said.
CLT-UFA is the product of the merger of Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) with UFA, the television unit of German media group Bertelsmann.
Belgian-Luxembourg media holding company Audiofina holds 49 percent of the company.

CLT-UFA is market leader in Germany, the Netherlands and the French-speaking southern half of Belgium. It is a large player in France and has started operations in radio and television in Britain. It is also active in Poland.
"We want to expand in several other northern and central European countries," Sautter said.

He said that besides the geographical expansion, the main goals of the new group included the development of pay television as a complement to free television, the building of a Europe-wide major position in television production and rights acquisitions and the further expansion of its radio business.
